questions.q: If A and B are two square matrices of the same order and $(\mathrm{AB}+\mathrm{BA})^{\mathrm{T}}+(\mathrm{AB}-\mathrm{BA})^{\mathrm{T}}=2 \mathrm{BA}$ then
options: A and B are both symmetric matrices but not skew symmetric matrices
A and B are both skew-symmetric matrices but not symmetric matrices
A and B are neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric matrices
$A$ and $B$ are any two non zero matrices
questions.solution:
$(A B+B A)^T+(A B-B A)^T=2 B A$
\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow(\mathrm{AB})^{\mathrm{T}}+(\mathrm{BA})^{\mathrm{T}}+(\mathrm{AB})^{\mathrm{T}}-(\mathrm{BA})^{\mathrm{T}} \\
& =2(\mathrm{AB})^{\mathrm{T}} \\
& =2\left(\mathrm{~B}^{\mathrm{T}} \mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\right)
\end{aligned}

If $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are symmetric $\Rightarrow \mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{A}$
then $2\left(B^T A^T\right)=2 B A$
and if both are skew symmetric then

\begin{aligned}
& A^T=-A, B^T=-B \\
& 2\left(B^T A^T\right)=2(-B \times-A)=2(B A)
\end{aligned}

$\therefore \mathrm{A}$ and B are both symmetric and skew symmetric.

questions.q: If $M$ and $N$ are square matrices of order 3 , then which one of the following statements is not true?
options: For all symmetric matrices $M$ and $N, M N-N M$ is skew symmetric
$N^{\top} M N$ is symmetric or skew symmetric according as $M$ is symmetric or skew symmetric
For all symmetric matrices $M$ and $N$, matrix $M N$ is symmetric
For any two matrices $M$ and $N$, adj $(M N)$ and adj (NM) need not be equal
questions.solution:
For two square matrices $M$ and $N$ of order 3 ,
the matrix $M N-N M$ is skew symmetric, if $M$ and $N$ are symmetric matrices, because
$\begin{aligned} & (M N-N M)^T=(M N)^T-(N M)^T \\ & =N M-M N=-(M N-N M)\end{aligned}$
The matrix $N^T M N$ is symmetric or skew symmetric according as $M$ is symmetric or skew symmetric, because $\left(N^T M N\right)^T=N^T M^T\left(N^T\right)^T=N^T M^T N= \begin{cases}N^T M N, & \text { if } M \text { is symmetric matrix } \\ -N^T M N, & \text { if } M \text { is skew symmetric matrix }\end{cases}$
The matrix $M N$ is not symmetric matrix for all symmetric matrices $M$ and $N$.
And for any two matrices $M$ and $N, \operatorname{adj}(M N)$ and $\operatorname{adj}(N M)$ need not be equal.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q:
If $A$ is a matrix such that
$\left[\begin{array}{ll}
2 & 1 \\
3 & 2
\end{array}\right] A\left[\begin{array}{ll}
1 & 1
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}
1 & 1 \\
0 & 0
\end{array}\right]$
then $A$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $\begin{aligned} & A=\left[\begin{array}{l}x_1 \\ x_2\end{array}\right] \\ & \therefore \quad\left[\begin{array}{ll}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x_1 \\ x_2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ &=\left[\begin{array}{c}2 x_1+x_2 \\ 3 x_1+2 x_2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ &=\left[\begin{array}{cc}2 x_1+x_2 & 2 x_1+x_2 \\ 3 x_1+2 x_2 & 3 x_1+2 x_2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad\left[\begin{array}{cc}
2 x_1+x_2 & 2 x_1+x_2 \\
3 x_1+2 x_2 & 3 x_1+2 x_2
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}
1 & 1 \\
0 & 0
\end{array}\right] \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x_1+x_2=1 \text { and } 3 x_1+2 x_2=0
\end{aligned}$
On solving, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& & x_1=2 \\
and & & x_2=-3 \\
& & A=\left[\begin{array}{r}
2 \\
-3
\end{array}\right]
\end{aligned}$
